source.org_or_authors: B. Blocken, J. Carmeliet (KU Leuven / TU Eindhoven)
source.quote: Traditional PMMA gauges performed better, indicating the presence of lesser adhesion water at this surface

rows.note: Qualitative: hydrophobic PTFE retained more adhered drops than PMMA. No underside/soffit catch ratio found.

gaps: Z-93 / AZ-93 / silicate thermal-control paint: no water contact angle, hysteresis, sliding angle or water uptake found (NASA NTRS, HII, Modus pages describe optics/composition only). A patent gives 15 deg for a potassium-silicate inorganic layer, not Z-93 (not recorded, patent not fetched).

Ultra-Ever Dry: manufacturer claim 160-175 deg only (press/vendor pages, not fetched in full); no sliding angle for NeverWet or Ultra-Ever Dry from a primary source. NRL report on commercial coatings (sliding angles with 5 uL drops) was found but not read.

Retained water per unit area (g/m2) after RAIN on painted metal, glass, polymer film, vehicle or aircraft skins, solar panels: none found. Only roof/paved depression-loss values (hydrology) and a condensation analogue.
Draining-film thickness of WATER after minutes: none found; Xue and Stone use silicone oil (tens of micrometres). Jeffreys formula recorded without a computed number.
Pendant (underside) drops: no measured maximum volume or mass for water hanging from a plate found; only capillary length 2.67 mm (warm water).
Underside versus top wind-driven rain catch ratio: no numbers found (Blocken and Carmeliet review gives facade catch ratios and gauge adhesion water only).

Furmidge relation with measured critical drop masses: the Furmidge Equation Revisited (PMC12080332) and the 1995 Corning drop-motion paper were found but gave no extractable critical-mass numbers (second is paywalled).
ITO advancing/receding angles: only static ~20-25 deg found; a patent gives bare ITO 20-80 deg depending on pretreatment (not fetched/recorded).
FEP film (Chemours) contact angle: datasheet gives no value; only the Daikin FEP coating value recorded. PTFE: only advancing 115 deg and a 5-15 deg hysteresis statement.
Silica/oxide overcoat on mirrors: only SiO2-on-silicon 20.7 deg; no sliding angles for oxide-coated mirrors found.
